subject: Physics
description: Pressure (P=F/A), atmospheric, fluid, Pascal's, Archimedes' principles

options.option_text: Mass times acceleration (F=ma)
Force per unit area (F/A)
Energy per unit time (work rate)
Mass per unit volume (density)

questions.explanation: PRESSURE P = F/A (force per unit area). Unit: PASCAL (Pa) = N/m². 1 atm = 101,325 Pa = 760 mmHg = 1.013 bar. Why a sharp knife cuts well: small contact area → high pressure. Why heavy trucks have wide tires: distribute weight over large area → less pressure on road. Distractor 1 = Newton's 2nd law. Distractor 3 = power. Distractor 4 = density.

questions.stem: ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE at sea level is approximately:

options.option_text: 10 kPa (much lower value)
101 kPa (1 atm = 760 mm Hg)
10,000 kPa (much higher value)
Zero Pa (vacuum at sea level)

questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure at sea level (1 ATM) = 101,325 Pa = 101.325 kPa = 760 mm Hg = 1.013 bar = 14.7 psi. Decreases with altitude (~1/2 every 5500 m). Mt. Everest: ~33% of sea level. Mariana Trench (10,994 m below sea level): ~1100 atm. Air pressure measured by BAROMETER (mercury column or aneroid). LOW pressure = stormy weather; HIGH pressure = clear / dry.
questions.subject: Physics

options.option_text: Heavy objects always sink in liquid
Buoyant force = weight of displaced fluid
Pressure rises with depth always
Liquids exert force in all directions

questions.explanation: ARCHIMEDES' principle: any object IMMERSED in fluid experiences UPWARD BUOYANT force = weight of fluid DISPLACED. Discovered by Archimedes in his bath (~250 BCE — he reportedly ran naked through Syracuse shouting 'EUREKA!'). Used to test if king's crown was pure gold (gold of given mass displaces less water than alloyed gold). FLOATING — buoyant force ≥ weight; SINKING — buoyant force < weight. Density of object < fluid density → floats. Steel ships float because hollow shape displaces water > ship's weight.
questions.subject: Physics

options.option_text: Heavier fluids exert more pressure than lighter ones at all depths
Pressure applied to enclosed fluid is transmitted equally everywhere
Liquids cannot be compressed at all under any condition
Hot fluids expand into cooler ones over time slowly

questions.explanation: PASCAL's LAW (Blaise Pascal, ~1646): pressure applied to enclosed fluid is transmitted UNDIMINISHED in ALL DIRECTIONS, equally to all parts of the fluid + walls. APPLICATIONS: HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS — small force on small piston → large force on big piston (mechanical advantage = ratio of areas). Used in: hydraulic brakes (cars), hydraulic jacks (lifting cars), hydraulic press, JCB / excavator arms, hydraulic lifts. Force out = (Area out / Area in) × Force in.

questions.stem: Why is it EASIER TO SWIM in SEA WATER than in fresh water?

options.option_text: Sea is calmer than rivers normally
Sea water is denser → more buoyancy
Sea water has currents to help swim
Sea is shallow at most coastal areas

questions.explanation: Sea water density ~1025 kg/m³ vs fresh water ~1000 kg/m³ (due to dissolved salts). Higher density → MORE BUOYANT FORCE on swimmer (Archimedes principle: buoyancy = ρ × V × g). Easier to FLOAT + SWIM in sea. EXTREME case: DEAD SEA (Israel-Jordan border) — ~33% salinity (vs ocean's ~3.5%) — density ~1240 kg/m³ → people FLOAT EFFORTLESSLY without effort. Also: hot air balloons + ships work on similar principle (less dense than surrounding fluid → float).
questions.subject: Physics

options.option_text: Ice is colder than water (lower temp)
Ice is less dense than liquid water
Ice is solid (denser than liquid usually)
Air bubbles are inside the ice always

questions.explanation: ICE density = 0.917 g/cm³; LIQUID WATER density = 1.000 g/cm³. UNUSUAL — water EXPANDS when freezing (most substances contract). Hydrogen bonding creates open hexagonal lattice in ice → less dense. So ice floats with ~10% above + 90% below water. CRITICAL for life: ice forms on top of lakes/rivers, insulating water below → fish + aquatic life survive winter. Without this property, water bodies would freeze from bottom up + kill marine life. ANOMALOUS EXPANSION OF WATER — water is densest at 4°C (not 0°C); above + below 4°C it's less dense.

questions.stem: Pressure of a fluid at depth h is given by formula:

options.option_text: P = h × A (height times area)
P = ρgh (density × g × depth)
P = m × g (just weight only) here
P = F × t (force × time) wrongly

questions.explanation: FLUID PRESSURE at depth h (below surface) = ρgh, where ρ = fluid density, g = gravity (~9.8 m/s²), h = depth. Independent of horizontal extent / shape of container. ALSO must add atmospheric pressure if open to air: P_total = P_atm + ρgh. WHY a swimmer's ear hurts at deep end: pressure increases with depth. Each ~10 m of water adds ~1 atm of pressure. Submarines designed for thousands of atm at deep ocean floor.
